author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are describing the disagreement that led to a mistrial after roughly a week of deliberations over whether she was criminally responsible for the 2023 deaths of her three children in Duxbury.

Five jurors have now spoken to news organizations, NBC 10 reported. Three, including the foreperson, said one member of the panel would not join the others in finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity. Another juror said the panel’s vote shifted as members reviewed evidence before most of them reached the same position.
The public accounts are the jurors’ descriptions of closed deliberations; they are not new court findings. Clancy remains charged, and the mistrial did not resolve guilt or criminal responsibility.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington has asked Judge William Sullivan to enter a not-guilty finding, arguing that prosecutors presented legally insufficient evidence of criminal responsibility. The defense is also pressing a double-jeopardy argument against another trial. A status conference is scheduled for September 29, when the judge is expected to consider the pending motions and the case’s next steps.
dek: Five panel members have spoken publicly after a week of deliberations failed to produce a unanimous decision on criminal responsibility.
headline: Jurors describe split that produced Lindsay Clancy mistrial
